closed_path.note: ClosedPath: a smooth closed loop on the ground plane (race track, patrol route, rail) with length, point/tangent at a distance, progress and lateral offset of any position, arc distance with wrap-around; plus yaw helpers (forward, right, yaw_of, wrap_angle) in the engine's convention (yaw 0 faces -Z).

multiplayer.note: Transport-agnostic authoritative server with explicit development/raw-UDP and production/QUIC-TLS profiles, 60 Hz authority, 20 Hz acknowledged deltas/keyframes, prediction, ownership, and combat. Protocol 8 rejects mismatched content; optional HMAC supplies client authentication on either profile. One authoritative registry owns session tokens and timeout cleanup; secure-random failures fail closed and keyed disconnects require credentials. GameState includes restart round and authoritative mover tick positions; sequenced commands from old rounds are discarded. Bounded partial-world replication retains one acknowledged baseline and one retryable packet per peer, respects active payload limits, rotates fair/priority records and peers, and exposes queue/delivery counters. Supports 1024 relevant records with individually budgeted records; replication and resync are bound to sessions (since protocol 7). See HOSTING.md for limits and RTT tradeoffs. Server capacity is configurable (with_max_players, --max-players); replication sizes candidates by arithmetic and prepares peers on several threads (with_network_threads, --network-threads) with identical bytes at any thread count (ADR 0027). Replication prioritises nearby records and measures freshness (mean_wait); the server takes time from a Clock so timeouts/reconnect are testable without sleeping; viewer::spans + be2-headless --profile report where a tick goes (ADR 0028). World updates (Snapshot/Delta) are a compact exact binary form, protocol 8, about 5x smaller per player record (ADR 0029). be2-headless stops cleanly on SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP (final autosave, exit 0; a second signal forces exit 130) without the ctrlc crate (ADR 0030). Stock protocol and shared transport/replication support remain for existing clients and hosts. New custom multiplayer games start with netplay (NetGame, ClientView, netplay::cli::serve), not the archived template.

contract.owns: Authoritative sessions and bounded acknowledged replication
contract.inputs: Bounded client intentions and transport outcomes
contract.performance: One baseline and one retryable packet per peer; active transport payload ceiling

constraints.text: Commit only exactly acknowledged represented state; budget each packet against the active transport limit. Queued bytes are not delivery.

JSON stdout stays stable; progress goes to stderr. perf.py record --suite check measures one full run without extra rebuilds. Generated games retain their own project checks. CI engine/game matrices run concurrently; early leo-images supports art review, while existing test guards require both matrices to succeed. Automatic check --changed --loop inner/integration selects whole-library units, declared transitive consumer suites and indexed Python checks; unknown/build-boundary inputs fail closed. Shipping remains the default. check --game reuses standalone project gates. context levels 1/2/3 expose guides, contracts and derived ownership; features --validate checks paths/edges/suites. dev_bench measures seven representative tool paths and one optional verification run; fresh-agent task evidence is separate. map authoring shares fresh headless itest outputs. start/next/resume provide build-free task routing and content-bound observed check evidence; notes never certify checks.

shared_gameplay.note: Standard new-game and stock --game consume playable::run_game_with_options: local HeadlessWorld authority without sockets, or server-owned state with shared prediction/interpolation. Authored objectives, timers, movers, dynamic props and win/restart run through the same simulation. Replication carries round identity and mover positions (since protocol 7). client_kit.note: Opt-in renderer parts for a game that draws its own world, each independent and without genre logic: View (camera, screen projection), Template/Batch/Tint (small meshes packed per frame into few draw calls), Look/Materials (lit + fog + glow world material, alpha and additive effects, sky; presets daylight/dusk/night), Fx (particles, rings, fireballs, beams, popups, banners), hud (scaled outlined text, panels, bars, vignette, crosshair), SoundBank (off-thread rendered effects and music stems, backend woken during loading, start_music/update_music glides each stem toward a target volume), capture::save_frame (reports the real pixel size). PlanarMirror owns a depth-backed target, off-axis aperture projection, near-plane clipping and reflection UVs. PointLight adds four bounded unshadowed local lights per pass, cleared by set_scene for compatibility. Shadows (ADR 0036): one setting (devkit::ShadowQuality Off/Simple/Full, default Simple, Settings.shadow_quality, --shadows flag, Esc > Settings via GameShell::local_menu_with_options) and one helper, kit::Shadows (begin_frame, blob, cast, apply, draw_decals). Simple is depth-tested contact blobs (Materials::decal with a clip-space depth bias, Batch::blob); Full is one texel-snapped directional shadow map of the key light (packed-depth RGBA8 target, normal-offset bias, 3x3 filter, key light only). examples/shadow_demo.rs is the runnable reference.

Rule conditions are counter comparisons, modulo and all/any/not (ADR 0023). Eligibility and presentation visibility are independent replicated states; hidden entities retain collision. Native game-describe/schema/validate/example; --game on client and headless. No scripting; movers translate authored gates. add-interactable creates a target's map and game records together (dry run unless --write). game-explore searches reachable rule states (winnable, shortest win/loss, dead rules, stuck states) using GameRuntime itself (ADR 0024). game-validate names the missing or mismatched map record of an interactable or mover; game-explore flags once-exhausted retries. Movers carry a grounded player standing on them (Controller::ride, ADR 0026). Optional stock presentation config sets objective/outcome wording, counter labels/visibility/units/clock, RGBA palette and bounded HUD; reads authority only. Canonical translate preserves exact box bounds after fractional edits. Schemas are generated from opt-in Rust types/constraints; maintain with be2.py schemas --write/--check (docs/SCHEMAS.md). Structural validity retains all existing semantic and shipping gates.

custom_simulation.note: For games whose rules are Rust, not GameDocument: enemies, projectiles, scoring, AI, waves, per-frame physics. Scaffold with new-game NAME DIR ENGINE_PATH custom-sim. Graphics-free devkit: FrameClock (wall-clock frame length; get_frame_time() is bumpy under vsync), FixedStepper, InputAccumulator (one input per tick, edges once), Simulation + StateHasher + assert_deterministic, Playback/Timeline/CapturePlan/PerfReport for --playback/--script/--capture/--perf, seeded Rng, Juice, atomic Settings/Records files (music/sfx volume and on/off toggles, downloads_dir, unique_path, sanitize_filename), Snapshot (save states: F5/F9, autosave, migrations, all-or-nothing loads), synth (procedural audio, including AmbientSpec/ambient_loop for seamless background music; `be2-tools ambient-music` generates one from the command line, see docs/AUDIO.md), wall_along_x/wall_along_z (straight walls with doorway gaps) and WaypointGraph (small branching graph, breadth-first path/nearest-node lookup) for a hand-built indoor level and the NPCs that move through it (ADR 0034). kit::Materials::draw_static(&meshes) binds the world material and draws a scene's static geometry in one call, so the two-step version cannot be called in the wrong order (silently renders nothing otherwise). TextField/CharFilter (sanitised typing and paste, caret, hold-to-repeat; ClientInput::feed_text / TextField::feed_frame add the keyboard and Ctrl+V clipboard glue) and resolve_ipv4/ServerChoice (typed server address to an IPv4 SocketAddr with player-facing errors; default server from --connect, server.txt, Settings::last_server, built-in). The game owns its single authoritative loop; do not stretch GameDocument into scripting.

geometry_kit.note: Procedural modelling for Template (kit::shape: Section/Ring/Sweep, Template::loft, sweep, rounded_box, capsule, rod, mirror_x, smooth_normals, offset_strip/offset_band/offset_path/strip_quads with mitred, curvature-clamped corners so a ribbon cannot fold over itself) and the geometry-defect lint (kit::lint: lint/lint_with/assert_clean/strip_folds/depth_resolution finding zero-area triangles, winding against normals, coplanar overlapping triangles of different parts = z-fighting, folded strips). View::camera_checked / view::depth_ratio_warning guard a far/near ratio over 3000. Lessons: coplanar quads z-fight, never offset per segment normal without a mitre and clamp, mind the depth ratio, fx_alpha/fx_add are never depth-tested.

ui_auditor.note: Headless 2D UI layout auditor validating all screens across 9 standard resolutions for overlap, text truncation, and responsive pause menu constraints.

netplay_hub.note: BEHB v2 advertises per-room transport and admission requirement. Production hub rooms reuse existing pinned QUIC/TLS, require join_key_env (exactly 32 bytes) and cli::serve hub_admission capability. Provision TLS pin/key and admission secrets outside discovery. hub::connect_room / connect_room_with_pin join with supplied ClientConfig; UDP discovery never distributes credentials. Development binds are loopback unless BLUE_ALLOW_DEVELOPMENT_INTERNET=1 explicitly permits trusted legacy deployments; helper rejects remote UDP. BEHB v1 gets update refusal; DFHB v1 remains for unkeyed development rooms; BECT remains v1. RoomManager health/terminate expose readiness, players, heartbeat, idle eligibility and graceful drain using existing Spawner/status/watchdog. Existing rollback/update tooling, bounded transport and reliable-event acknowledgements remain. deploy/hub/update.sh and tools/hub_deploy.py retain dependency-aware identities, exact artifact receipts, atomic promotion, readiness checks and receipt-matched rollback recovery. Interrupted rollback resumes before skipping rejected source; it never rebuilds that rejected source.

contract.owns: Game-agnostic serving of netplay games: the shared server main and its machine formats, the hub protocol, the registry, room processes and ports, abuse limits, the legacy Deadfall protocol adapter, and the game-side hub client

contract.outputs: A hub that players list and create rooms on, and rooms that are ordinary netplay servers
contract.performance: One datagram each way; replies at most 1000 bytes and at most five times the padded request; about 5 MB per idle room process

netplay.note: Online play for custom-sim games. NetGame supplies rules, layouts and seats; ClientView supplies prediction and interpolation; NetServer/NetClient supply lobby, sessions, input bundles, snapshots, events, bot handoff, per-match telemetry (matches.jsonl) on any DatagramTransport (UDP, QUIC/TLS, in-memory LoopNet). net::codec is the bounds-checked binary Writer/Reader. A failed connect is a typed NetClient::failure() (ConnectFailure: Unreachable/VersionMismatch/WrongKey/MatchInProgress/Full/Other) with a player-facing hint(). Extracted from Spooky Kart; toy.rs is the smallest complete game. New multiplayer starting point: src/viewer/netplay/toy.rs (NetGame + ClientView), src/bin/be2-toy-server.rs (netplay::cli::serve). Old multiplayer template is archived, not recommended. Opt-in RELIABLE_EVENTS separates authenticated, sequenced event delivery from state; bounded retention exposes gaps. lobby_capacity/minimum_players gate room seats and countdown. snapshot_with_budget lets games trim optional effects to the active path budget.

contract.owns: Lobby, sessions, input streaming, snapshot pacing, event delivery, bot handoff and match statistics for a game
contract.inputs: A NetGame implementation and a DatagramTransport
contract.outputs: An authoritative match and clients that predict and interpolate
contract.performance: One snapshot per client every SNAPSHOT_EVERY ticks, within the active transport ceiling (at most 1,100 bytes); up to four bounded reliable-event retries per snapshot.

save_state.note: Native save states for every tier. One framed, versioned file (SHA-256 over every byte, atomic write with a last-good .bak, named slots, autosave ring, payload migrations, content-fingerprint binding); engine worlds (HeadlessWorld::save_bytes/restore_bytes: players, rules, props, lifecycle; not rapier internals) with a checksum-verified, all-or-nothing restore; GameSession F5/F9 and --load/--save-dir in the stock client; DedicatedServer::with_autosave and be2-headless --load/--autosave; devkit::Snapshot for custom simulations with assert_resumes_exactly, and for physics-backed ones (ADR 0018: contact caches are unsaved history, isolated by experiment) assert_loads_replay_identically plus assert_resumes_within; the promise is declared once as Snapshot::POLICY (SavePolicy::Exact or PhysicsContinuation, ADR 0019), recorded in every save, shown by save-info and proved by assert_resumes_as_promised, which the starter's save test calls; Simulation::hash_parts makes a failed restore name the differing part; be2-tools save-info. What happens after a load depends only on the file. Online clients never save.

contract.owns: The save file format, atomic writes, slots and backups, verification, migrations, world capture/restore, and the all-or-nothing load
contract.inputs: A running HeadlessWorld or Snapshot simulation; save-file bytes
contract.outputs: Framed save bytes, typed SaveError naming the differing hash part, a restored simulation identical to the saved one (and to the uninterrupted run where physics is at rest or falling)
contract.performance: One JSON pass each way; a Test Lab world saves in single-digit milliseconds

constraints.text: A save never replaces a good file with a partial one, and a file whose bytes do not verify is never loaded.

game_shipping.note: Every game ships as a package with its own identity, by script: assets/identity.json (title, tagline, controls, packaging), a title-seeded icon set (be2-tools icon TITLE DIR [VARIANT] [--replace]) used as the exe resource icon (build.rs + rc.exe), the window icon, dist/<exe>.ico and the shortcut icon, scripts/ship.py package/shortcut/verify/ship, an optional requested desktop shortcut named after the game that targets dist/ (never target/), tooltip = tagline + controls, verified by reading it back, rendering the shell icon, optionally advising on icon similarity, and launching through it. scripts/check.py ends with display-independent package integrity/resources without desktop access; ship or verify --smoke runs isolated graphical verification; --skip-ship iterates without it, no desktop is reported as skipped, never as a pass. Package verification is display-independent: strict portable manifest paths, every SHA-256, complete declared source inventory when available, and GameDocument.map closure. Graphical smoke copies only declarations outside the checkout and saves full stdout/stderr; mutable player files are preserved in dist but excluded from smoke. Package-only ship --no-install; verify --folder or --check-shortcut requests installation. verify --icon-similarity is advisory only; unrelated installed applications cannot fail shipping.
checks: generated project: scripts/blue ship into a temp folder, then verify --launch --smoke (real window title and icon read back)

rendering_traps.note: Template::quad_facing winds a quad to face a normal whatever the corner order; Template::split and Batch::add split a template over the per-mesh vertex limit (9,000) instead of dropping it; a Template past 65,535 vertices panics instead of wrapping its u16 indices. A world that renders as an empty void was one of these.

audio_authoring.note: Named audio projects: be2-tools audio describe/validate/render/check. JSON effect cues (23 presets and variants, authored stereo scores, imported 44.1kHz PCM16 WAV), music (authored scores, generated base/melodic/lead stems or ambient), MIDI notes, equal-power pan, ADSR and optional lowpass. Strict ranges, bounded synthesis, wrapped releases, shared attenuation protects any adaptive layer subset, peak/RMS/DC/seam evidence and checked content hashes. AudioBank::load loads reusable rendered bundles on a worker; named play/music, explicit Loading/Ready/Muted/Empty/Failed states and errors. Edit data and rerender without Rust rebuild or music regeneration at startup. Native audio_preview provides cue controls and layer fades. audio_report.py --loop evaluates actual wrapped continuity instead of one-shot zero endpoints; clipping, silence, DC, loudness, spectrograms remain measured. No live voice pitch/spatial API, device audibility acknowledgement or sample-clock synchronization claim. Existing SoundBank and synthesis APIs remain supported. Stock GameDocument presentation.audio binds counter changes/threshold crossings, success/failure/restart to cues, and authoritative counters to adaptive music levels. Loaded game paths resolve assets without cwd dependence; --mute skips asset/device loading; settings toggles persist. Local fixed-tick observation preserves catch-up transitions; online snapshots are observed state, not a reliable event stream. Imported clips support exact-length adaptive looping ambience with a bounded wrap crossfade, stereo preservation and worst-subset headroom. Leo uses recorded nature and a separate original score, driven by authoritative day/night state; edits need rendering, not a Rust rebuild. Linux/Windows native playback uses the engine-owned quad-snd patch: unavailable hardware and worker failures produce explicit BackendState::Unavailable, never gameplay authority. Validate/render/check resources without hardware; Ready/submission is not audible playback.

contract.owns: Data-authored effects and music, crossfaded imported ambience loops, reusable checked PCM bundles, named presentation playback and numeric quality evidence
contract.inputs: Versioned AudioProject JSON, seed, optional imported WAV and read-only game events, optional presentation.audio state bindings
contract.outputs: PCM16 stereo assets, bank metadata, diagnostics and playback submissions
contract.performance: Render before shipping; worker reads/checks assets, bounded decoder submissions per poll

checks: Feta furniture passages, solid legs/undersides, Scientist exclusion, four-map desks
dropped-prop overlap recovery for both characters; wall exclusion and stable feet
movement.note: Keep frame-rate independence and render/headless parity. Controller floor is optional (set_floor(None) for voids), gravity is settable, apply_impulse adds a decaying push for knockback; see docs/CONTROLLERS.md.

learning_loop.note: How the engine learns from the games built on it (ADR 0038): python tools/learn.py record writes a friction entry (cost, workaround, trap, copied code) to docs/learning/ledger.jsonl; dupes finds code the games copied and checks whether the engine already has it; eval scores be2.py context against a task benchmark (recall, packet size); sessions (local only, never committed) aggregates where AI effort went from session logs without storing any content; modules refreshes the per-file summaries context routes by; report writes docs/learning/REPORT.md. be2.py context appends matching ledger traps and "already solved by" lines. record --keywords supplies retrieval terms; missing terms warn archive-only. Promote solved entries in place while retaining history and replace obsolete workaround/hint. All four tuned development fixtures protect aggregate and individual discovery results, without appending evaluation history in tests.

idea_forge.note: IdeaForge CLI generates a fresh mechanic with Codex, has an AI build the actual native BlueEngine game, independently executes behavioral/package gates and reviews its capture, waits for exact-source Linux/Windows and installer CI, publishes to BlueEngineGames, verifies public downloads and commits AI-authored feedback to the engine learning ledger. Isolated worktrees preserve user edits; retained phase state resumes failures; transcripts remain private. The curated idea browser is a separate legacy utility. Daily scheduling reserves one 2D and one 3D publishing run per local date in random order, retries retained work and prevents duplicates. Published artifacts remain immutable while a separate journaled engine-integration worktree merges concurrent main and delivers feedback. Changed relevant source requires new game CI; unchanged source reuses the exact original game receipt. Resume reconciles lost Git push responses and preserves append-only feedback; terminal slug conflicts require a new run identity.
